stem: Which gas is known as ‘noble gas’?
expl: The noble gases make a group of chemical elements (Group 18 in periodic table) with similar properties under standard conditions. They are all odourless, colourless, monatomic gases with very low chemical reactivity. These gases generally do not undergo chemical reactions under certain given conditions. The six noble gases that occur naturally are Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe) and the radioactive Radon (Rn).

stem:
Which of the following gasses is/are lighter than air ?
1. Hydrogen chloride
2. Sulfur dioxide
3. Helium
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
expl: At the same temperature and pressure, the density of a gas is proportional to its molar mass (M). The average molar mass of dry air is taken to be about 28.97 g/mol. A gas with molar mass less than this is considered lighter than air. Among the given gases, hydrogen chloride (about 36.5 g/mol) and Sulfur dioxide (about 64 g/mol) have molar masses greater than dry air, whereas helium (about 4.0 g/mol) has a much lower molar mass than dry air. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

stem: Which gas is not in the gaseous cycle ?
expl: Biogeochemical cycles can be classed as gaseous in which the reservoir is the air or the oceans (via evaporation), and sedimentary in which the reservoir is Earth's crust. Gaseous cycles include Nitrogen, Oxygen, Carbon and Water. Sedimentary cycles include Iron, Calcium, Phosphorus, Sulfur and other more earthbound elements.

stem: Which of the following pair of gases is used for the respiratory activities of divers?
expl: The deep sea divers carry cylinders which contain a mixture of oxygen and helium (called 'Heliox'). The presence of helium in this mixture generates less airway resistance than air and thereby requires less mechanical energy to ventilate the lungs. Helium is much less soluble in water than many other gases, such as nitrogen. The low solubility means it does not enter the blood stream even under pressure.

stem: What is the shape of Sulfur hexafluoride molecule?
expl: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF ) is an inorganic, colourless, odourless and non-flammable compound. SF molecule has an octahedral shape, consisting of six fluorine atoms attached to a central Sulfur atom.

stem: Easily soluble in water –
expl: Ammonia being a polar molecule dissolves readily in water. This is due to the hydrogen atoms of ammonia which are bonded with a highly electronegative nitrogen and the hydrogen atoms of water molecules which are bonded with the highly electronegative oxygen atom. Ammonia and water are both polar molecules and they are both capable of hydrogen bonding, so they are highly miscible.

stem: Which is used as Laughing gas –
expl: Nitrous oxide (N O) is also known as laughing gas. It is a colourless gas with a slight metallic odour and taste. Its inhalation leads to disorientation, euphoria, numbness, loss of coordination, dizziness and ultimately a loss of consciousness. It is also used as the anaesthetic gas. This gas is used in medical and dental procedures as a sedative. It helps to relieve anxiety before the procedure and allow the patient to relax.

stem: Which one of the following is also called Stranger Gas?
expl: Xenon is a gaseous element with symbol Xe and atomic number 54. It is a rare, odourless, colourless and tasteless gas. It is also known as Stranger Gas. It is a noble gas of Group 18 in periodic table and although generally unreactive, it can undergo a few chemical reactions. Its volume is very low in the atmosphere (about 0.08 parts per million). It was discovered in England by the Scottish chemist William Ramsay and British chemist Morris Travers in 1898.

options.label: a

options.label: c

expl: The nitrogen cycle is a process by which nitrogen is converted into its various chemical forms. This transformation can be carried out through both biological and physical processes. The nitrogen cycle includes fixation, ammonification, nitrification and denitrification. Denitrifying bacteria converts nitrate and nitrite ions into nitrogen. From discharge of this nitrogen, its amount in the lithosphere and in atmosphere remains unchanged.

stem: Which one of the following is the permanent gas in the atmosphere?
expl: Permanent Gases are those gases which are believed to be incapable of liquefaction and remains gaseous under normal conditions. These gases include hydrogen, nitrogen, carbon monoxide etc. Nitrogen is a permanent gas in the atmosphere. It accounts for about 78% of the atmosphere.

stem: The gas used to inflate the tyres of an aircraft is –
expl: Nitrogen gas is used in the tyres of an aeroplane.This is because the nitrogen gas does not support combustion and can assist in preventing wheel fire when the aircraft lands (braking and high speed can produce dangerously high temperatures) unlike in oxygen. There are other benefits but effectively it is being the lowest cost gas that does not support combustion.

stem: In order to compensate the deficiency of which of the following elements, the insectivorous plants trap and eat insects ?
expl: Carnivorous or insectivorous plant can trap and digest insects and other small animals. They do this to obtain vital nitrogen that they need to grow. Most of the plants absorb enough nitrogen from nitrates in the soil.

stem: The soil in which insectivorous plants grow is deficient in :
expl: Insectivorous plants cannot take their nitrogen from soil as they grow in waterlogged swampy soils deficient in nitrogenous compounds. Such plants obtain their nitrogen from small insects. For this work, these plants have evolved special mode of nutritions. Example of insectivorous plants are Nepenthes, Dionea, Drosera, Utricularia, etc.

stem: Which gas is usually filled in the balloon?
expl: A gas balloon flies in the air because it is filled with a gas which is lighter than air. Helium is mostly used in gas balloons. It is also inert in nature and does not form an explosive mixture with air.

stem: Tear gas is :
expl: Tear gas is a chemical weapon that causes severe eye and respiratory pain, skin burning, vomiting and even blindness. In the eye, it stimulates the nerves of the lacrimal gland to produce tears. It is mostly used by the police force in controlling riots. Alphachloroacetophenone, 2-chlorobenzalmalononitrile and acrolein are generally used as tear gas. Chlorine (Cl) is used as reagent in synthesis of tear gas.

stem: The foul smell of dead fish is due to the compound :
expl: Trimethylamine is a tertiary amine that is structurally an amino compound in which every hydrogen atom of ammonia is replaced by a methyl group. The odour (smell) of dead fish is due to the presence of these compounds.

stem: Which of the following remains in a solid state at normal temperature?
expl: The Group 7 elements are also known as the halogens. They include fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine which all have 7 electrons in their outer shell. Iodine is a bluish-black solid with a metallic lustre, thus it remains in a solid state at normal temperature.

stem: The most reactive among the halogens is –
expl: The halogens (Fluorine, Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine, Astatine) are non-metal elements which are highly electronegative and reactive. They constitute Group 17 of the periodic table. The newly created element Tennessine (Ts) with atomic number 117 also belongs to this group, but its chemical properties are still unknown. Fluorine is the smallest atom among the halogen elements. It also has the strongest ability to attract electrons from other elements making it the most reactive of the halogens.

expl: Bromine is a member of halogen group of elements. It is a fuming red-brown liquid at room temperature that evaporates readily to form a similarly coloured gas.

stem: Which one of the following elements exist in liquid state at room temperature?
expl: Bromine is an element with symbol Br and atomic no. 35. It is the third lightest halogen and is a fuming liquid with deep red colour. It is the only non-metallic element to exist in the liquid state at room temperature.

stem: The halogen being used as analgesic is –
expl: Analgesic drugs act in various ways on the peripheral and central nervous system. Compounds of bromine are used as analgesics.

stem: Which one of the following non-metals is not a poor conductor of electricity?
expl: Selenium is a non-metallic photoconductive substance. It demonstrates photovoltaic action. Gray selenium is a semiconductor showing appreciable photoconductivity. It becomes more electrically conductive when it absorbs electromagnetic radiation or light. Selenium exists in several allotropes that interconvert upon heating and cooling carried out at different temperatures and rates. Element number 34, Selenium was discovered by Swedish chemist Jons Jacob Berzelius in 1817.

stem: The most commonly used substance in fluorescent tubes are –
expl: Fluorescent lamp tube is generally filled with a gas containing low pressure mercury vapor and argon. Sometimes other inert gases like xenon, neon or krypton are also used. The pressure inside the lamp is around 0.3% of atmospheric pressure.

stem: Which gas is filled at low pressure in a tubelight?
expl: The normal tubelights are filled with mercury vapour with inert gases like argon or neon. An electric current in the gas excites mercury vapour which produces short wave ultraviolet light that causes phosphor coating inside the bulb to glow.

stem: The gas used in discharge tubes for optical decoration and advertising is –
expl: The neon gas is used in discharge lamps, tubes and in fluorescent bulbs.
